352655.title: The $a\equiv3\pmod 4$ Stirling valuation conjecture
352655.statement:
Let $f(b,c)=\sigma_2(b)-\sigma_2(c)+\nu_2\left(\binom{2c-b-1}{c}\right)$, where $c3_2$ is the binary digit sum and $bd_2$ is the $2$-adic valuation. Let $a,b,c,h$ be positive integers satisfying $c>b\ge1$ and $3\le a\le2^{h-1}$ with $a\equiv3\pmod 4$. **The $a\equiv3\pmod 4$ conjecture.** One has

$$
\nu_2\left(S\left(c2^h+2,b2^h+a\right)\right)=\sigma_2(a)+f(b,c)+\nu_2\left(\binom{a+1}{2}\right)-1.
$$

The claim is motivated by numerical experimentation and extends the theorem's lower bound in the residue class $a\equiv3\pmod4$; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
352655.source_name: Arnold Adelberg and Tamas Lengyel, “New results on the p-adic valuation of Stirling numbers”, arXiv:2111.08766 (2021).
352655.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08766

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2021).

353030.title: A supercongruence relating two cubic binomial sums
353030.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $r$ a positive integer. Define

$$
S_{p,r}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p^r-1}x^k\sum_{j=0}^k {2j\choose j}^3{2k-2j\choose k-j}^3(3j+1)(3k-3j+1).
$$

**The supercongruence.**

$$
S_{p,r}\left(\frac1{16}\right)-S_{p,r}\left(-\frac18\right)\equiv0\pmod{p^{2r+2}}.
$$

This strengthens the two preceding congruences, each of which has modulus $p^{r+2}$, by asserting extra cancellation in their difference.
353030.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo and Long Li, “q-Supercongruences from squares of basic hypergeometric series”, arXiv:2112.12076 (2021).
353030.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

353195.title: Baruah–Begum conjecture on congruences for the smallest parts function of restricted overpartitions
353195.statement:
Let $\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega(n)$ denote the smallest-parts function of restricted overpartitions. For integers $\ell\geq1$, $k\geq0$, and $n\geq0$, consider its values at the indicated arithmetic progressions. **Baruah–Begum's conjecture.** For any $\ell\geq1$, $k\geq0$ and $n\geq0$, 

$$
\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2k+\ell-1}(10n+5)\right)\equiv \overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{\ell-1}(10n+5)\right)\pmod{5^\ell},
$$

and

$$
\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2\ell}(10n+3)\right)\equiv\overline{\operatorname{spt}}_\omega\left(5^{2\ell}(10n+7)\right)\equiv0\pmod{5^{2\ell}}.
$$

These conjectured congruence families extend congruences previously proved by Baruah and Begum modulo small powers of $5$ for the restricted-overpartition smallest-parts function.
353195.source_name: Dazhao Tang, “A conjecture of Baruah and Begum on the smallest parts function of restricted overpartitions”, arXiv:2201.01642 (2022).
353195.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

355133.title: Congruence conjecture for permanents of the absolute-difference matrix
355133.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $\delta_{jk}$ be the Kronecker delta, and let $\operatorname{per}(M)$ denote the permanent of a matrix $M$. **Absolute-difference permanent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{per}[|j-k|+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant p}\equiv \frac{1}{2}\pmod p.
$$

The conjecture is presented as being inspired by a related congruence for $\operatorname{per}[|j-k|]$ and by the paper's determinant evaluation. The source gives no evidence that this assertion has been resolved.
355133.source_name: Han Wang and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Evaluations of some Toeplitz-type determinants”, arXiv:2206.12317 (2023).
355133.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.12317

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

356252.title: Positivity conjecture for copartition parity differences
356252.statement:
Let $a,b,m\in\mathbb{N}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Let $\mathrm{cp}_{a,b,m}^e(n)$ and $\mathrm{cp}_{a,b,m}^o(n)$ denote the numbers of $(a,b,m)$-copartitions of $n$ with an even and odd number of ground parts, respectively. **Positivity conjecture.** If $b\mid a$, then

$$
\mathrm{cp}_{a,b,m}^o(n)\leq \mathrm{cp}_{a,b,m}^e(n).
$$

Equivalently, the $q$-series

$$
\frac{(-q^{a+b};q^m)_\infty}{(-q^a;q^m)_\infty(q^b;q^m)_\infty}
$$

has non-negative coefficients when $b\mid a$. This generalizes the $(1,1,2)$ case; the claim is known when $a=b$, and a special case with $(a,b,m)=(3,1,4)$ follows from work of Craig. A combinatorial proof beyond the established cases remains open.
356252.source_name: Hannah E. Burson and Dennis Eichhorn, “On the positivity of infinite products connected to partitions with even parts below odd parts and copartitions”, arXiv:2209.13784 (2022).
356252.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.13784

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

358163.title: Vanishing bound for Romik's sequence $d(n)$ modulo primes $p\equiv3\pmod4$
358163.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $e\ge1$, and let $(d(n))_{n\ge0}$ be the sequence defined in the paper. **The third conjecture.**

$$
d(n)\equiv0\pmod{p^e}
$$

for $n\ge\left\lceil\frac{ep^2}{4}\right\rceil$.

This is proposed as an analogous improvement of the paper's vanishing theorem for $d(n)$; no proof or resolution is given.
358163.source_name: Christian Krattenthaler and Thomas W. Müller, “The congruence properties of Romik's sequence of Taylor coefficients of Jacobi's theta function θ_3”, arXiv:2304.11471 (2024).
358163.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11471

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

358661.title: An odd-parameter supercongruence for a terminating hypergeometric sum
358661.statement:
Let $r\leq 1$ be an odd integer coprime with $5$, and let $p$ be an odd prime such that $p\equiv r\pmod{5}$ and $p\geq (5-3r)/2$. Then **the proposed supercongruence.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(10k+r)\frac{(\frac{r}{5})_k^5}{(1)_k^5}\equiv\frac{p\Gamma_p(\frac r5)^4}{\Gamma_p(\frac{2r}5)^2\Gamma_p(\frac12+\frac{3r}{10})\Gamma_p(\frac12-\frac r{10})^3}\sum_{k=0}^{(1-r)/2}\frac{(\frac{r-1}{2})_k(\frac r5)_k^3}{(1)_k(\frac{2r}5)_k^2(\frac12+\frac{3r}{10})_k}\pmod{p^5}.
$$

This is presented as an open conjecture motivated by a preceding theorem and numerical evidence; its validity remains unresolved in the source.
358661.source_name: Chen Wang, “Supercongruences arising from a _7F_6 hypergeometric transformation formula”, arXiv:2306.02635 (2023).
358661.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02635

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

360461.title: A fifth-order q-supercongruence
360461.statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $n\equiv1\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}4)$, and let $(a;q)_k$ denote the q-shifted factorial. **The fifth-order q-supercongruence conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{mn-1}(-1)^k[4k+1]\frac{(q;q^2)_k^4(q^2;q^4)_k}{(q^2;q^2)_k^4(q^4;q^4)_k}q^k
\equiv [n]\frac{(q^2;q^4)_{(n-1)/4}^2}{(q^4;q^4)_{(n-1)/4}^2}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}(-1)^k(4k+1)\frac{(\frac12)_k^5}{k!^5}\;\allowbreak(\operatorname{mod}\Phi_n(q)^3).
$$

The $m=1$ case was previously given by the author; the conjecture is described as a simplified version of earlier conjectures.
360461.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo, “Dwork-type q-congruences through the q-Lucas theorem”, arXiv:2310.15207 (2023).
360461.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15207

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2023).

361205.title: Weak primary pseudoperfect strongly pseudoperfect uniqueness conjecture
361205.statement:
A **weak primary pseudoperfect number** is a positive integer $n$ satisfying

$$
\frac{1}{n}+\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{1}{p}\in\mathbb{N},
$$

where the sum is over the prime divisors of $n$. A strongly pseudoperfect number is understood in the sense defined in the paper. **Weak primary pseudoperfect uniqueness conjecture.** The only weak primary pseudoperfect number that is also strongly pseudoperfect is $6$. The source notes that weak primary pseudoperfect numbers may be more numerous than primary pseudoperfect numbers and suggests that this conjecture would be substantially harder to prove.
361205.source_name: Tim McCormack and Joshua Zelinsky, “Weighted Versions of the Arithmetic-Mean-Geometric Mean Inequality and Zaremba's Function”, arXiv:2312.11661 (2024).
361205.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

362111.title: The distinct-prime-divisor conjecture for Mersenne-type numbers
362111.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer divisible by $\ell$ distinct primes, and suppose that

$$
\gcd(2^n-1,n)=1.
$$

**Distinct-prime-divisor conjecture.** If $\ell\geq 3$, then $2^n-1$ is divisible by at least $2^\ell$ distinct primes.

The preceding lemma gives only the lower bound $2^\ell-1$ in the case $p=2$; the authors state this stronger bound because they have no examples attaining $2^\ell-1$ when $\ell\geq 3$.
362111.source_name: Silvio Dolfi, Roghayeh Hafezieh and Pablo Spiga, “On the structure of the character degree graphs having diameter three”, arXiv:2402.19335 (2024).
362111.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

362288.title: Solvabilizer number of PSL2 for prime powers congruent to one modulo four
362288.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power satisfying

$$
q\equiv 1 \mod 4.
$$

Set $G=\operatorname{PSL}_{2}(q)$.

**PSL2 congruence conjecture.**

$$
\alpha(G)=q.
$$

This is proposed as a further generalization of the theorem for $\operatorname{PSL}_{2}(2^f)$ and is supported in the paper by the computational table.
362288.source_name: Banafsheh Akbari, Tuval Foguel and Jack Schmidt, “Solvabilizer Numbers of Finite Groups”, arXiv:2403.08129 (2024).
362288.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08129

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362564.title: Complete congruence system conjecture for the Erdős–Straus conjecture
362564.statement:
Let $p\in\mathbb{N}$ be prime, and let $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$. Consider the two congruence conditions

$$
p\equiv -4d \pmod{4dn-1}\qquad\text{or}\qquad p\equiv -n \pmod{4dn-1}.
$$

**Complete congruence system conjecture.** For every prime $p$, there exist $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that at least one of these congruences holds. If true, this congruence system covers all primes and implies the Erdős–Straus conjecture. The claim is motivated by experimental evidence and by the characterizations of Type A and Type B solutions stated immediately before it; no proof or disproof is supplied in the source.
362564.source_name: Miguel Angel Lopez, “A Complete Congruence System for the Erdos-Straus Conjecture”, arXiv:2404.01508 (2024).
362564.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01508

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362918.title: The conjectured RH inequality for primes congruent to 3 modulo 8
362918.statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be primes with $p\equiv q\equiv 3 \pmod 8$, satisfying $0<2a<p<q$, and let $\chi_q(p)=\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)$ be the Legendre symbol modulo $q$. Let $$ denote the equation referenced in the source. **RH inequality conjecture.** The relation $$ holds for all such primes $p$ and $q$. The source gives no resolution; the relation is intended as a criterion connected with the Riemann Hypothesis.
362918.source_name: Brian Conrey, “Character Sums and the Riemann Hypothesis”, arXiv:2404.19647 (2024).
362918.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19647

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2024).

363818.title: The base-$p$ digit-sum conjecture for planar monomial exponents
363818.statement:
Let $q=p^n$, and write $s_p(m)$ for the sum of the base-$p$ digits of the positive integer $m$. Let $e\star d$ denote the operation used in the source on the exponents modulo $q-1$. **Base-$p$ digit-sum conjecture.** For every positive integer $d\leq q-1$ satisfying

$$
d\not\equiv 1\pmod{p-1},\qquad d\not\equiv\left\lfloor\frac{p+1}{2}\right\rfloor\pmod{p-1},
$$

there exists a positive integer $e\leq q-1$ such that

$$
s_p(e\star d)-s_p(e)>\frac{n(p-1)}{2},
$$

unless either $s_p(d)=2$, or $p=5$, $n$ is odd, and $d=5^j(5^i+1)/3$ for some non-negative integers $i,j$. The conjecture is motivated by computations and is relevant to the classification of planar monomials. The source gives no resolution evidence, so its status remains open.
363818.source_name: Christof Beierle and Tim Beyne, “A degree bound for planar functions”, arXiv:2407.04570 (2025).
363818.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04570

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

364499.title: The Jacobi-symbol conjecture for the integers $c_p$
364499.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For $\delta\in\{0,1\}$, define

$$
D_p^{(\delta)}(w)=\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)+\left(\frac{jk}{p}\right)w\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}-\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}.
$$

For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted by the preceding theorem through $D_p^{(0)}(w)=-w((p-1)c_p/2)^2$; for $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted through $D_p^{(1)}(w)=w(c_p\sum_{k=1}^{(p-1)/2}(\frac{k}{p}))^2$.

**Jacobi-symbol conjecture for $c_p$.** For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\left(\frac{p}{c_p}\right)=1,
$$

where $(\frac{p}{c_p})$ is the Jacobi symbol.

The conjecture is based on numerical values of $c_p$ listed in the source. The supplied text gives no resolution or proof, so its status remains open.
364499.source_name: Deyi Chen and Zhi-Wei Sun, “On determinants involving (j^2-k^2p) and (jkp)”, arXiv:2408.14401 (2024).
364499.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.14401

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

366674.title: A q-analogue of the Van Hamme–Sun supercongruence equivalence
366674.statement:
Let $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ be a positive integer. Define the $q$-integer $[m]=(1-q^m)/(1-q)$, the $q$-shifted factorial $(x;q)_k=(1-x)(1-xq)\cdots(1-xq^{k-1})$, and let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial. **q-analogue conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[6k+1]\frac{(q;q^2)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{3k^2} \equiv \sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(-1)^k[8k+1]\frac{(q;q^4)_k^3}{(q^4;q^4)_k^3}q^{2k^2+k} \pmod{[n]\Phi_n(q)^3}.
$$

This is a proposed $q$-analogue of an equivalence between two supercongruences for primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$; its validity for all positive integers $n\equiv1\pmod4$ remains open.
366674.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo and Chen Wang, “Refinements of Van Hamme's (E.2) and (F.2) supercongruences and two supercongruences by Swisher”, arXiv:2501.09626 (2025).
366674.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09626

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

366806.title: Factor 4 conjecture for Markov-polynomial coefficients
366806.statement:
Let $\rho=a/b$ be rational, and let the critical triangle be the set of lattice points satisfying

$$
i<a,\qquad j<b,\qquad \frac{i}{a}+\frac{j}{b}>1.
$$

Consider the coefficients of the Markov polynomial associated with these lattice points. **Factor 4 conjecture.** Every coefficient of a Markov polynomial corresponding to a lattice point strictly within the critical triangle is divisible by $4$. The conjecture is based on experimental data about coefficients in the critical-triangle region; the source gives no resolution.
366806.source_name: S. J. Evans, A. P. Veselov and B. Winn, “Arithmetic and geometry of Markov polynomials”, arXiv:2501.14882 (2025).
366806.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14882

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).

367325.title: Conjecture on shifted periodicity of Hankel determinants for Motzkin convolution powers
367325.statement: Let $F(x,r)=M(x)^r$, where $M(x)$ is the generating function of the Motzkin numbers, and let $H_n(F(x,r))$ be its Hankel determinants. The conjecture asserts that, for $r\equiv 0\pmod 3$, the shifted period of $H_n(F(x,r))$ is $r$, whereas, for $r\equiv 1$ or $2\pmod 3$, its shifted period is $3r$. This summarizes the periodic patterns predicted by the preceding formulas for the Hankel determinants of Motzkin convolution powers.
367325.source_name: Ying Wang and Yingrui Zhang, “Hankel determinants for convolution powers of Motzkin numbers”, arXiv:2502.21050 (2025).
367325.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21050

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).

372149.title: Baruah and Sarma's sign conjecture for coefficients of Rogers–Ramanujan products
372149.statement:
Let

$$
\frac{1}{R^{5}(q)}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}A(n)q^{n},\qquad R^{5}(q)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}B(n)q^{n},\qquad \frac{R(q^{5})}{R^{5}(q)}=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}D(n)q^{n},
$$

where

$$
R(q)=\frac{(q;q^{5})_{\infty}(q^{4};q^{5})_{\infty}}{(q^{2};q^{5})_{\infty}(q^{3};q^{5})_{\infty}}.
$$

**Baruah–Sarma sign conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq 0$,

$$
A(5n)<0\quad(n\neq 0),\qquad B(5n)<0\quad(n\neq 0),\qquad D(5n+1)>0.
$$

The cases $A(0)$ and $B(0)$ are excluded because $A(0)=B(0)=1>0$. The conjecture concerns the sign patterns of coefficients of higher-order Rogers–Ramanujan products; the surrounding results establish related eventual sign patterns, while these three inequalities were presented as numerical conjectures.
372149.source_name: Bing He and Xiongze Zhang, “Proof of a conjecture of Baruah and Sarma on sign patterns of certain infinite products”, arXiv:2512.17195 (2025).
372149.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

372890.title: Odd-multiple valuation conjecture for inert Gaussian power sums
372890.statement:
Let $p\ge7$ be a prime with $p\equiv3\pmod4$, and write $n=r(p-1)$ with $r\ge1$. **Odd-multiple valuation conjecture.**

$$
v_p\!\bigl(\mathbf G_{r(p-1)}(p)\bigr)=\begin{cases}0,&r\text{ even},\\3,&r\text{ odd}.\end{cases}
$$

Equivalently, among multiples of $p-1$,

$$
v_p(\mathbf G_n(p))=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{lcm}(4,p-1)\mid n,
$$

for $p\equiv3\pmod4$, and outside this locus the valuation is $3$. The mod-$p$ behavior is known in the stated range, but the asserted valuation $3$ for odd multiples, including all $r\ge p$, remains conjectural.
372890.source_name: Nikita Kalinin and Faith Shadow Zottor, “A p-adic (p34) depth-5 supercongruence for Gaussian p-th power sums over a square”, arXiv:2602.00206 (2026).
372890.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

373310.title: Conjecture on Euler liars and Carmichael or Sophie Germain pseudoprimes
373310.statement: Let $n$ be an odd squarefree composite integer, and let Euler liars in $\mathbb{Z}_n^*$ mean the elements $a$ satisfying the Euler probable-prime congruence $a^{(n-1)/2}\equiv \left(\frac{a}{n}\right)\pmod n$. **Euler-liar count conjecture.** If $n$ has $\varphi(n)/2$ Euler liars in $\mathbb{Z}_n^*$, then $n$ is a Carmichael number; and if it has $\varphi(n)/4$ Euler liars in $\mathbb{Z}_n^*$, then $n$ is either a Carmichael number or a Sophie Germain pseudoprime. The claim proposes a classification of odd squarefree composites with especially many Euler liars; its resolution is left as future work in the source.
373310.source_name: Alejandra Alcantarilla Sánchez, Jolijn Cottaar, Tanja Lange and Benne de Weger, “Ours go to 211: Euler pseudoprimes to 47 prime bases (from Carmichael numbers)”, arXiv:2602.21840 (2026).
373310.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21840

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2026).

373547.title: Monomial congruence counting conjecture
373547.statement:
Let $a,b,c$ be non-zero integers with $a,b,c$ setwise coprime, and let $d\geqslant 1$ be another integer. For a prime $q\geqslant 3$, define $N_{a,b,c,d}(L,M,N;q)$ to count triples $(l,m,n)\sim L\times M\times N$ satisfying

$$
(l^a m^b n^c)^d\equiv 1\pmod q,
$$

but with $l^a m^b n^c\ne 1$. **Monomial congruence counting conjecture.** There exists $\eta_0>0$, depending on $a,b,c,d$ but not on $q$, such that for every $L,M,N\geqslant 1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
\frac{N_{a,b,c,d}(L,M,N;q)}{\sqrt{LMN}}\ll_{\varepsilon,a,b,c,d}q^\varepsilon\left(\frac{\sqrt{LMN}}{q}+(LMN)^{-\eta_0}\right).
$$

This estimate is the conjectural input needed to control error terms in the cubic moment analysis and would establish the expected asymptotic lower-bound equality in the general case. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or refuted.
373547.source_name: Étienne Fouvry, Emmanuel Kowalski, Philippe Michel and Will Sawin, “Toroidal families and averages of L-functions, II: cubic moments”, arXiv:2603.10746 (2026).
373547.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10746

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

373736.title: Parry and non-Parry powers conjecture for roots of $x^d-x^{d-1}-1$
373736.statement:
For each integer $d\geq2$, let $4\theta_d4$ be the relevant root of

$$
x^d-x^{d-1}-1=0.
$$

For $d\equiv5\pmod 6$, use the noncyclotomic factor as specified in the source. A **Parry number** is a real number greater than $1$ whose greedy expansion of $1$ is eventually periodic.

**Parry-power conjecture.** For every $d\geq6$, $4\theta_d4$ is Parry, and for every integer $k\geq2$, $4\theta_d^k4$ is non-Parry.

The claim is introduced after computational tests for the family and is presented as a conjecture. No proof or resolution is supplied.
373736.source_name: Kevin G Hare and Hachem Hichri, “Parry order of Parry numbers”, arXiv:2603.19554 (2026).
373736.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19554

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2026). “The algebraic characterization of Parry numbers remains an open problem.”

374072.title: The characterization of strongly matchable numbers by M-numbers
374072.statement: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ denote its set of divisors and let $\tau(n)=|D(n)|$. Say that $n$ is **strongly matchable** if every coprime arithmetic progression of $\tau(n)$ integers admits a coprime matching to $D(n)$. Say that $n$ is an **M-number** if it is not divisible by any $p^p$ for a prime $p$, equivalently if $v_p(n)\leq p-1$ for every prime $p$. **The strong matchability characterization conjecture.** A number $n$ is strongly matchable if and only if it is an M-number. This would give an exact structural characterization of strong matchability, extending the preceding results on ordinary matchability and its asymptotic density. The statement is presented without resolution evidence in the source.
374072.source_name: Nathan McNew and Carl Pomerance, “Matchable numbers”, arXiv:2604.05304 (2026).
374072.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05304

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

374120.title: Andrews–Dixit–Schultz–Yee oddness conjecture for a double Lambert series
374120.statement:
Let

$$
Y(q):=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^m q^{2nm+m}}{(1-q^{2m-1})(1+q^n)}.
$$

Here $q$ is a complex number with $|q|<1$, so the double Lambert series defines an analytic function in its domain of convergence. **Andrews–Dixit–Schultz–Yee conjecture.** The function $Y(q)$ is odd:

$$
Y(-q)=-Y(q).
$$

The conjecture was proposed as an alternative route to proving the congruences for the overpartition function $\overline{p}_\omega(n)$ at arguments $4n+3$ and $8n+6$. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source material.
374120.source_name: Su-Ping Cui and Dazhao Tang, “Identities and transformations for Lambert series and double Lambert series”, arXiv:2604.08839 (2026).
374120.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08839

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

374432.title: The coefficient characterization conjecture for divisor-sum congruences
374432.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonnegative integers satisfying $0\leq B<A$, and let $N=An+B$. Define $\sigma_0(m)$ to be the number of positive divisors of $m$. Suppose that, for every nonnegative integer $n$,

$$
\sum_{1\leq k<\sqrt{N}}\sigma_0(N-k^2)\equiv0\pmod4.
$$

**The coefficient characterization conjecture.** Under this assumption, $A\equiv0\pmod4$ and $B\equiv2\pmod4$.

This conjecture is based on a computational observation about pairs $(A,B)$ for which the displayed congruence holds throughout the authors' search range. The phenomenon is not explained by the approach of the paper or by the previously mentioned work, so the asserted necessity of these congruence conditions remains open.
374432.source_name: Sittinon Jirattikansakul, Teeradej Kittipassorn, Kraiwich Kongsiri, Nitipon Moonwichit and Kirati Sriamorn, “Congruences via Partitions with Exactly Two Part Sizes”, arXiv:2604.25394 (2026).
374432.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25394

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2026).

374837.title: Amdeberhan–Andrews–Ballantine coefficient identity for a double Lambert series
374837.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. The notation $[q^n]A(q)$ denotes the coefficient of $q^n$ in the series $A(q)$. **Amdeberhan–Andrews–Ballantine coefficient identity.**

$$
[q^{2r}]\sum_{m,n\geq1}\frac{q^{2mn}}{(1+q^{2n-1})(1-q^{2m-1})}=[q^{2r}]\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{(n-1)q^n}{1+q^{2n-1}}.
$$

The identity was proposed as one of two conjectures used in the study of generalized and double Lambert series, and as a route toward a conjecture of Andrews, Dixit, Schultz and Yee. The source states that it has since been proved by the first author and Tang.
374837.source_name: Su-Ping Cui, Rahul Kumar and Aman Singh, “Two Proofs of a Conjecture of Amdeberhan, Andrews and Ballantine for double Lambert series and a new Representation for E_2(q)”, arXiv:2605.21163 (2026).
374837.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21163

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Very recently, Conjecture and Conjecture have been proved by the first author and Tang .”

375404.title: Sun's conjecture on the new constant $w_r(n)$
375404.statement:
Let $n>1$ and $r>0$ be integers. Define $w_r(n)$ as the least positive integer $k$ such that, for any $k$ integer vectors ${\bf a}_i=(a_{i1},\ldots,a_{ir})$ not congruent to ${\bf 0}=(0,\ldots,0)$ modulo $n$, there is an $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that 
$$
\sum_{i\in I}{\bf a}_i\equiv{\bf 0}\pmod n
$$
 but 
$$
\sum_{i\in I}{\bf a}_i\not\equiv{\bf 0}\pmod {n^2}.
$$
 **Sun's conjecture.** Let $n>1$ be an integer. (i) For any $2n-1$ integers $a_1,\ldots,a_{2n-1}$ not divisible by $n$, there is an $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2n-1\}$ with $|I|\in\{n,n+1\}$ such that $\sum_{i\in I}a_i$ is divisible by $n$ but not divisible by $n^2$. (ii) We have $w_2(n)=4n-3$. These claims are motivated by the preceding exact results for $w_1(n)$ and by the equality $s(\mathbb Z_n^2)=4n-3$; the source reports them as conjectures based on computation, with no resolution supplied.
375404.source_name: Zhi-Wei Sun, “On zero-sum problems of new types”, arXiv:2606.18234 (2026).
375404.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18234

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

381482.title: A q-congruence for the central trinomial coefficient
381482.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime with $p\geq 5$. Define the $q$-analogue of the trinomial coefficient by

$$
\left({n\choose j}\right)_q=T_1(n,j,q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}q^{k(k+j)}{n\choose k}_q{n-k\choose k+j}_q,
$$

where $[n]_q=(1-q^n)/(1-q)$ and $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the integral part of the real number $x$. **The q-congruence conjecture.** One has

$$
\left(2p\choose p\right)_q\equiv\left(2\left\lfloor\frac{p+3}{6}\right\rfloor+p\right)(q^p-1)+2\pmod{[p]_q^2}.
$$

This is proposed as a $q$-analogue of the preceding trinomial congruence, motivated by numerical calculation; its validity is left as a problem for further research.
381482.source_name: Moa Apagodu and Ji-Cai Liu, “Congruence properties for the trinomial coefficients”, arXiv:1907.13547 (2019).
381482.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.13547

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

381971.title: 2-adic valuation conjecture for Ā at k=2 and powers of 2
381971.statement:
Let $A_{\overline{\mathcal K},k,m}(0)$ denote the relevant constant term. **2-adic valuation conjecture at $k=2$.** For every integer $a\geq2$,

$$
\operatorname{ord}_2\left(A_{\overline{\mathcal K},2,2^a}(0)\right)=2a+7.
$$

This is an empirical special case of the prime-power investigations in the source and is not proved there.
381971.source_name: Barry Brent, “On the constant terms of certain meromorphic modular forms for Hecke groups”, arXiv:2212.12515 (2022).
381971.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.12515

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
